personas.summary: The authoring in this package is among the strongest accessibility work I have reviewed on this platform: every one of the 26 figures carries a chemistry-bearing alt text plus a genuinely structural long description, all 156 hints are text, every selectable option carries a compound name alongside its structure, the prose teaches by atom-numbering rather than by pointing at pictures, and — critically — both reaction_coordinate_reasoning items describe their profiles purely geometrically (relative heights, climb measured from the preceding valley) without ever stating step count, rate-determining step, overall classification or per-step classification. I verified the arithmetic behind both descriptions and they are correct and leak-free; the ch22 leak class has been cleanly avoided. The problem is delivery, not authoring. Three hard barriers stand between this package and a non-visual learner: (1) the authored `accessible_description` on all 52 questions is compiled and resolved into the activity envelope but no student-facing surface ever reads it; (2) the one renderer that tries — the reaction-coordinate renderer — reads the wrong key (`description` instead of `accessible_description`) and falls back to the aria-label "Schematic reaction coordinate diagram", leaving a blind student asked for four readings of a diagram they cannot perceive at all; (3) the four blank-canvas drawing items are delivered as an embedded Ketcher iframe whose own type manifest declares `keyboard_complete=False`, with the promised `structured_molecule_entry` fallback unimplemented. Separately, the reader compiler silently drops all 26 asset `long_description`s and all 10 nugget `practice_check` blocks, so the richest non-visual content in the package never reaches a reader at all. These are platform gaps, not authoring failures, but they are load-bearing here and the chapter should not publish over them.

location.anchor_text: Four carbonyl compounds are shown as structures: benzaldehyde, propanal, cyclohexanone, and ethyl acetate.

findings.observation: Every one of the 52 questions carries an authored `accessibility_bundle.accessible_description`, and it survives compilation into `compiled/question-set.json` and is resolved into the activity envelope as `accessibilityBundle` ([internal source reference — not in this repo], [internal source reference — not in this repo]). No student-facing surface reads it. A repo-wide search for `accessibilityBundle` in frontend/src returns only the type declaration, a demo-envelope stub that hardcodes `null`, a public-demos API type, and ReactionCoordinateQuestionRenderer (which reads the wrong key — see access-002). Neither LmsWorkspacePanel, PublicQuestionSetPanel, ActivityWorkspaceRenderer, nor any of the fifteen per-type renderers this chapter uses reference it. The only page that renders an accessible description is the question-type demo gallery ([internal source reference — not in this repo]), which serves platform demo fixtures, not this bank. The reader-side static preview, frontend/public/reader/topic-chapters/carbonyl-condensation.questions.json, strips `student_config`, `feedback_bundle` and `accessibility_bundle` entirely, keeping only `prompt_text`.
findings.learner_impact: A learner using a screen reader receives the prompt and whatever the individual renderer happens to expose, and nothing else. For most items in this chapter that is survivable because every option carries a text name — but it is survivable by accident, not by design. The author's deliberate stimulus descriptions ('Two acetaldehyde molecules are shown side by side, with five labelled atoms…', 'Five selectable sites are offered — the carbanion carbon, the enolate oxygen…') are written to be the non-visual equivalent and are simply discarded. For the two reaction-coordinate items the loss is total (access-002).
findings.evidence: Authored: `accessibility_bundle.accessible_description` on all 52 entries in topic.package.json `question_sets[]`. Compiled: present on all 52 entries in compiled/question-set.json. Resolved: `accessibility_bundle=question.accessibility_bundle or None` ([internal source reference — not in this repo]). Consumed: `grep -rn accessibilityBundle frontend/src` → [internal source reference — not in this repo], [internal source reference — not in this repo] (`null`), [internal source reference — not in this repo], [internal source reference — not in this repo] only.
findings.recommended_outcome: Every question a student can be assigned needs its authored accessible description to actually reach the student — as programmatically-associated text on the workspace, not only as an aria-label on one figure. Until the delivery path exists, this chapter's non-visual equivalence is asserted rather than provided.

location.anchor_text: The profile below describes acetone being converted to a conjugated enone on warming with base. Answer the questions about the profile.

findings.observation: The reaction-coordinate renderer draws the profile as an inline `<svg role="img">` whose aria-label is `envelope.question.accessibilityBundle?.description` with the fallback string "Schematic reaction coordinate diagram" ([internal source reference — not in this repo]). The authored key is `accessible_description`, not `description`, so the lookup always misses and the fallback always wins. Because `role="img"` removes the SVG's children from the accessibility tree, the in-diagram `<text>` labels ('Acetone (2 equivalents)', '‡', 'Aldol addition product', 'Conjugated enone + H₂O') and every y-coordinate are also unreachable. The prompt adds no geometry. Both `ch23-aldol-dehydration-profile` and `ch23-aldol-dehydration-profile-v2` then require four readings: step count, rate-determining step, overall classification, and a classification per step.
findings.learner_impact: A blind or low-vision student is asked to report which climb is larger and whether each step is uphill or downhill from a graphic announced to them only as 'Schematic reaction coordinate diagram'. The task is not merely harder — it is unanswerable except by guessing. Both advanced items on the aldol-condensation-dehydration concept are affected, and this is the only place in the chapter where the required information exists exclusively in a picture. The irony is that the author wrote exactly the description that would fix it (the 'climb measured from the valley immediately before it' phrasing is precisely right); it is discarded by a key mismatch.
findings.evidence: Compiled question `accessibility_bundle` = `{"accessible_description": "A free-energy profile is presented… whose climb measured from the valley immediately before it is smaller than the first climb measured from the start…"}`. Renderer: `aria-label={(envelope.question.accessibilityBundle?.description as string | undefined) ?? "Schematic reaction coordinate diagram"}` (line 148). Profile control points carry the only quantitative information: ts_1 y=18, min_1 y=4, ts_2 y=20 (v1); ts_1 y=15, min_1 y=-6, ts_2 y=12 (v2).
findings.recommended_outcome: The two energy-profile items need their stationary points, relative heights and per-step climbs available as text to a non-visual learner at the moment of answering; the diagram cannot remain the sole carrier. A key-name mismatch between authoring and rendering must not be able to silently void an authored equivalent.

location.anchor_text: Draw the aldol addition product formed when acetaldehyde is treated with dilute sodium hydroxide.

findings.observation: Four required items — ch23-draw-aldol-product, ch23-draw-aldol-product-v2, ch23-draw-dieckmann-product, ch23-draw-dieckmann-product-v2 — use `structure_scaffold` with `student_config.scaffold = "blank_canvas"`. The platform's own type manifest is explicit that this is not keyboard-reachable: `AccessibilityBlock(keyboard_complete=False, # honest: Ketcher canvas is not yet ([internal PRD reference — not in this repo]), nonvisual_response_mode="structured_molecule_entry", requires_molecule_description=True)` ([internal source reference — not in this repo]). [internal source reference — not in this repo] and a link to open the same surface full-screen; it implements no text/SMILES entry, and the declared `structured_molecule_entry` mode appears nowhere in the renderer. The answer is captured solely from `postMessage` events emitted by canvas manipulation.
findings.learner_impact: A student who cannot use a pointing device, or who cannot see the canvas, cannot submit an answer to these four items at all — not a degraded answer, no answer. Both mitigating factors are real but partial: neither affected concept is assessed only by drawing (aldol-reaction also has single_select, bond_change_ledger and curved_arrow items; dieckmann-cyclization also has two numeric_with_units items), and the answer keys are plain SMILES that a text field could accept. That makes this a delivery gap rather than a design gap — but as shipped it is a required activity some learners cannot complete.
findings.evidence: `{"scaffold":"blank_canvas"}` on all four items; answer keys `CC(O)CC=O`, `CC(=O)CC(C)(C)O`, `CCOC(=O)C1CCCC1=O`, `CCOC(=O)C1CCCCC1=O`. [internal source reference — not in this repo]. [internal source reference — not in this repo] has no input element of any kind.
findings.recommended_outcome: Every drawing item in this chapter needs a non-pointer, non-visual way to submit the same structure — the type manifest already names the need (`structured_molecule_entry`) and the graders already accept SMILES, so the equivalent path is missing rather than impossible. Until it exists, these four items should not be assignable as required work.

location.anchor_text: Two carbons. The right-hand carbon is double-bonded to an oxygen and carries a single hydrogen; that is the carbonyl carbon, the electrophilic site.

findings.observation: All 26 assets carry an `accessibility.long_description` averaging ~380 characters of genuine atom-by-atom readout. None of them reaches the reader. `[internal source reference — not in this repo]accessibility.alt_text` and then sets the card's visible `description` to the asset's `learning_goal`. `grep -c long_description frontend/public/reader/topic-chapters/carbonyl-condensation.json` returns 0, and `grep -rn long_description tools/` shows the topic-package pipeline never reads the field at all — it is authored into a dead end.
findings.learner_impact: Non-visual learners get the alt text, which in this chapter is unusually good, but lose the layer that actually teaches: which carbon is alpha and why, which bond is the new one, how the product maps back onto the two starting molecules. The loss is worst on the structurally complex figures — mol-wieland-miescher-ketone's long description explains which shared carbon is quaternary and which carbonyl was consumed by the closure, information the 172-character alt text cannot carry. Sighted learners lose it too, since the reader card renders alt text visibly as 'Described as: …'.
findings.evidence: 26/26 assets have non-empty `accessibility.long_description` in topic.package.json. [internal source reference — not in this repo]; :84 `"description": asset.get("learning_goal", "")`. Zero occurrences of `long_description` or of the string 'Two carbons. The right-hand carbon' in the compiled reader chapter.
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter needs the authored structural readouts to be deliverable to readers who need more than a one-sentence alt text; content written specifically as the non-visual equivalent must not be discarded at compile time.

location.anchor_text: Which bond breaks in the retro-aldol direction, and what single compound results?

findings.observation: All 10 nuggets carry a `practice_check` with a prompt and a full worked answer. The deck-creator compilation emits them as 'Check your understanding' slides (10 occurrences in frontend/public/deck-creator/carbonyl-condensation.json), but the reader compilation drops them entirely: `grep -c practice_check frontend/public/reader/topic-chapters/carbonyl-condensation.json` returns 0, and the reader's block-type inventory is only external_link (10), mcmurry_link (1), molecule (36), text (10), video (5).
findings.learner_impact: The practice checks are the chapter's only fully text-native, self-scoring retrieval opportunity — no canvas, no drag, no diagram, every one answerable and checkable by reading. They are exactly the surface a learner using assistive technology can use independently, and they are exactly what the reader omits. A reader-only student (the common case, since the question bank sits behind teacher preview) gets ten sections of prose and 36 figures with no checkpoint at all.
findings.evidence: 10/10 nuggets have `practice_check.prompt` + `.answer` in topic.package.json; e.g. nugget-robinson-annulation: 'why can the intramolecular aldol condensation not simply be run first…'. [internal source reference — not in this repo] emits them for the deck; [internal source reference — not in this repo].
findings.recommended_outcome: The reader needs the authored practice checks to reach the student; a text-only self-check is the least-mediated form of practice this chapter offers and it currently exists only on a surface students do not see.

location.anchor_text: The task is to report how many steps the profile shows, identify which step controls the rate, and classify each step and the overall reaction from these features.

findings.observation: Both reaction-coordinate items ask for `step_count` *and* `rate_determining_step` *and* `step_types`. The renderer builds the rate-determining-step dropdown from `Array.from({length: stepCount})` ([internal source reference — not in this repo], 230) and renders one 'Step n' row per step for `step_types` (line 262). With `profile.step_count = 2`, the student sees exactly two RDS options and exactly two step-type rows before answering anything — so the UI discloses the answer to the step-count question it is simultaneously asking.
findings.learner_impact: Affects every learner equally, so it is not an access inequity, but it voids one of the four readings each item claims to assess and it does so invisibly to the author (the compile-time leak guard inspects text, not renderer geometry — I ran `find_accessibility_leaks` over all 52 compiled questions and it returns zero flags). It also means the accessible-description work that so carefully avoids stating the step count is protecting an answer the interface gives away.
findings.evidence: `"ask":["step_count","rate_determining_step","overall","step_types"]` and `"profile":{...,"step_count":2,...}` on both items. Renderer: `const steps = Array.from({length: stepCount}, (_, i) => i + 1);` then `{steps.map((n) => <option …>Step {n}</option>)}` for RDS and `{steps.map((n) => …)}` for the step-type rows.
findings.recommended_outcome: An item that asks a student to count the steps needs an interface that does not pre-count them; either the count must not be asked alongside the per-step readings, or the per-step controls must not be sized from the answer.

location.anchor_text: The task is to decide which one lacks any hydrogen on a carbon adjacent to its carbonyl group and is therefore confined to the acceptor role in a condensation.

findings.observation: Several accessible descriptions restate the task using the very criterion the item is testing, rather than describing the stimulus and the ask. ch23-acceptor-only-partner's prompt asks only 'which can serve only as the acceptor, never as the donor'; the description supplies the operational rule ('lacks any hydrogen on a carbon adjacent to its carbonyl group'). ch23-donor-or-acceptor-only does the same ('classify each compound by whether a base can remove a proton from a carbon adjacent to its carbonyl group'), as does ch23-rank-michael-donors ('reasoning from the number and type of neighbouring carbonyl groups'). Contrast ch23-clean-mixed-aldol-partners, where the same phrasing is a fair gloss of the prompt's own word 'non-enolizable'.
findings.learner_impact: This is the inverse of the usual leak: it does not name the answer, but it converts a two-step inference ('acceptor-only ⇒ no enolate ⇒ no alpha H') into a one-step lookup, and it does so only for the learner reading the accessible description. That learner is assessed on a materially easier item than the sighted learner beside them. Because these are the chapter's core-difficulty items on its foundational concept, the mis-measurement lands where it matters most.
findings.evidence: ch23-acceptor-only-partner prompt vs description as quoted; ch23-donor-or-acceptor-only description 'classify each compound by whether a base can remove a proton from a carbon adjacent to its carbonyl group'; ch23-rank-michael-donors description '…reasoning from the number and type of neighbouring carbonyl groups.'
findings.recommended_outcome: Accessible descriptions across these items need to convey what is shown and what is asked without also supplying the discriminating rule, so that the non-visual and visual versions of an item are the same item.

location.anchor_text: Assemble the two-stage Robinson annulation that converts 2-methylcyclohexane-1,3-dione into the fused bicyclic enone shown as the target.

findings.observation: In both Robinson route items the target and two of the four intermediates are labelled only by non-specific descriptors: 'the fused bicyclic enone', 'the bicyclic ketol, before loss of water', 'the saturated bicyclic diketone', 'the bicyclic diol from exhaustive reduction'. RouteBuilderRenderer renders each structure with `alt={entry.text}` (StructureCard, line 53), so those strings are the whole non-visual representation. The accessible description adds nothing beyond 'a fused bicyclic enone is the target'. Every other item in the chapter names its structures in IUPAC — including the sibling Stork route items, whose intermediates are '1-(cyclohex-1-en-1-yl)pyrrolidine' and '2-(3-oxobutyl)cyclohexan-1-one'.
findings.learner_impact: A non-visual learner cannot tell which bicyclic enone is the target — ring sizes, the position of the enone, the quaternary methyl are all unstated. The task remains completable, because the route is fully determined by the reagent sequence, but the student is reasoning from reagents alone while a sighted student reasons from the target structure. On the chapter's capstone concept that is a meaningful difference in what is being assessed.
findings.evidence: `target_structure: {"text":"the fused bicyclic enone", "structure_smiles":"CC12CCC(=O)C=C1CCCC2=O"}`; intermediates `m_ketol` text 'the bicyclic ketol, before loss of water', `m_saturated` text 'the saturated bicyclic diketone'. StructureCard: `<Box as="img" src={imageUrl} alt={String(entry.text ?? caption)} …>`. The package already holds a full description of this exact structure in asset mol-wieland-miescher-ketone.
findings.recommended_outcome: The Robinson route items need their target and intermediates identified specifically enough that a learner who cannot see the drawings knows which compounds they are choosing among.

location.anchor_text: Complete the reasoning: how many atoms are in the ring formed by the closing stage? Give a digit or a word.

findings.observation: Both robinson structured_reasoning items place the answer to their free-text sub-question inside one of their own evidence options. In -v2 the `reasoning` field asks for the ring size (accepted answers '6', 'six', 'six-membered') while evidence option `e_six` reads 'A six-membered ring closure requires exactly that five-atom spacing' — and `e_six` is itself a required correct selection. In v1 the `reasoning` field asks for the class of compound revealed (accepted answers '1,5-diketone', '1,5-dicarbonyl') while required evidence option `e_15` reads 'A conjugate addition always leaves the two carbonyl groups in a 1,5-relationship'.
findings.learner_impact: Affects all learners equally rather than being an access barrier, so I flag it as adjacent to my remit rather than central to it. The effect is that the third field of each item measures reading rather than reasoning, which matters because these are the two advanced items carrying the chapter's synthesis-level objective. I note it here because the compile-time leak guard cannot see it (it compares the accessible description against the answer key, not the answer key against the student config) and it is the same failure mode as an accessible-description leak, one field over.
findings.evidence: ch23-robinson-retrosynthesis-v2: `reasoning.answer_text` includes '6','six','six-membered'; `evidence` option e_six text 'A six-membered ring closure requires exactly that five-atom spacing'; `expected_option_ids` includes 'e_six'. ch23-robinson-retrosynthesis: `reasoning.answer_text` includes '1,5-diketone'; e_15 text 'A conjugate addition always leaves the two carbonyl groups in a 1,5-relationship'; e_15 is expected.
findings.recommended_outcome: The free-text rung of these two items needs to require something the student must supply, not something already printed among the options they are asked to tick.

location.anchor_text: Open on two acetaldehyde molecules, colour-coded: the left one tinted as the future donor, the right one as the future acceptor

findings.observation: Four of the five video briefs make colour the sole carrier of a chemical distinction in their storyboards: donor vs acceptor by tint (video-aldol-mechanism), the conjugated pi system by shading (video-e1cb-dehydration), the leaving group by tint (video-claisen-mechanism), and the two fused rings plus the shared edge by differential tint (video-robinson-two-stages). Each brief's `production_note` records a requirement for closed captions, narration naming every visual change, and a transcript — but no requirement that a colour distinction be redundantly encoded. The briefs are `production_status: "deferred"` and the compiled reader marks all five video blocks `is_hidden: true` ([internal source reference — not in this repo]), so nothing is shipped broken today.
findings.learner_impact: Prospective rather than current. If these are produced against the storyboards as written, a colour-blind learner loses the donor/acceptor assignment in the aldol video and the ring-fusion reading in the Robinson video — the two single most important pieces of information in each. The alt-text and prose work elsewhere in this chapter is careful about this; the briefs are the one place it lapses.
findings.evidence: Storyboard lines quoted above from video_briefs[0].storyboard[0], [1].storyboard[4], [2].storyboard[2], [4].storyboard[5]. `production_note` text: 'closed captions plus narration naming every visual change … and a text transcript' — no colour-redundancy clause. Compiled reader video blocks carry `"url": ""` and `"is_hidden": true`; [internal source reference — not in this repo] returns null for hidden blocks, so no dead 'Watch' control is exposed.
findings.recommended_outcome: The production requirements recorded on these briefs need to include a non-colour encoding for every distinction the storyboard currently makes by tint, so the requirement is captured before the videos are made rather than found afterwards.

location.anchor_text: Acetaldehyde: a partner that can play both roles

findings.observation: The reader's heading hierarchy skips a level throughout. TopicPackageChapterRenderer emits the chapter title as `h1` and each section title as `h2`; every block card in ReaderBlockRenderer is then an `h4` (lines 179, 290, 368, 390, 498, 525, 567). No `h3` is produced anywhere, and the section prose contains no markdown headings of its own.
findings.learner_impact: Screen-reader users navigating by heading level get an h2→h4 jump at every one of the 36 figure cards in this chapter, which reads as a missing level of structure and makes 'jump to next sibling section' behave unpredictably. Minor, and platform-wide rather than specific to this chapter, but it is 36 instances here.
findings.evidence: [internal source reference — not in this repo] (`as="h1"`), :140 (`as="h2"`); [internal source reference — not in this repo] returns only h4. Compiled chapter has 10 sections and 62 blocks, 36 of them molecule cards.
findings.recommended_outcome: Reader figure and link cards need to sit one level below their section rather than two, so heading navigation reflects the actual document structure.

location.anchor_text: The diethyl malonate anion is shown beside but-3-en-2-one.

findings.observation: The reference structures embedded in three interactive question types carry generic alt text supplied by the renderer rather than by the item: CurvedArrowRenderer uses `alt="Reaction system for this arrow question"` (line 246) and ErrorRepairRenderer uses `alt="Structure for the flawed step"` (line 116). BondChangeLedgerRenderer is the exception and does better, falling back to the item's own `reaction_display` string.
findings.learner_impact: Low, because in every affected item this chapter supplies the chemistry through labelled controls instead — the curved-arrow items enumerate sites as 'Ring alkene carbon farther from the carbonyl group (beta carbon)', and both error_repair items put the full plan in `flawed_work` text including the condensed formula. So the tasks stay completable. What is lost is the ability to inspect the drawn structure itself, which a sighted student can do freely.
findings.evidence: [internal source reference — not in this repo]; [internal source reference — not in this repo]; [internal source reference — not in this repo]. Affected items: ch23-aldol-attack-arrow(+v2), ch23-michael-arrow(+v2), ch23-flawed-claisen(+v2).
findings.recommended_outcome: The reference figure inside an interactive item needs a description of that specific structure, not a description of the question type — the ledger renderer already shows the pattern.

strengths: Both reaction_coordinate_reasoning items describe their profiles in purely geometric terms and state none of the four things they ask for. I checked the arithmetic: v1 (ts_1 18 from 0, ts_2 20 from a valley at 4) gives climbs of 18 and 16, and the description says the second maximum 'stands slightly higher above the starting level than the first' but its 'climb measured from the valley immediately before it is smaller' — correct, and it yields RDS=1 by derivation rather than by disclosure; v2 (climbs 15 and 18) is described just as accurately in the opposite direction. Step count, rate-determining step, overall classification and per-step classification are all derivable and none is stated. This is the ch22 leak class cleanly avoided.

All 26 asset alt texts convey actual chemistry rather than naming the image — 'Ethyl acetoacetate: an ester and a ketone separated by a single CH2 group', 'A fused bicyclic diketone: two six-membered rings sharing an edge, one carrying a conjugated enone and the other a saturated ketone, with a methyl group at the ring fusion'. The reader also renders alt text visibly as 'Described as: …', so it benefits everyone.

Nine of the fifteen question types this chapter uses are keyboard-complete in code, which I verified renderer by renderer: rank_order (per-card up/down IconButtons with aria-live position readout), matching_pairs and categorize_groups (one labelled Select per item), comparison_matrix (Selects in a table with scope="col"/"row"), synthesis_route (Selects per step), bond_change_ledger (Selects plus a text field, with `<Th scope>` headers), curved_arrow (source/target Selects — the registry's 'electron_action_list' mode actually implemented), error_repair (RadioGroup + Selects), structured_reasoning (CheckboxGroup + Selects + text).

Every selectable option in the chapter carries a `text` name alongside its `structure_smiles`, and SelectedResponseRenderer sets the option image's alt to that name — so all 12 single_select, 4 multi_select and 2 matching_pairs items are answerable from names without seeing a structure. This is consistent across all 52 items with no exceptions.

The curved_arrow site labels and the bond_change_ledger atom labels are semantic, not positional: 'Carbanion alpha carbon of the malonate anion (lone pair)', 'The proton that water delivers to the acceptor's oxygen'. A learner who cannot see the drawing can still reason about which site is which.
All 156 hints across the bank are `kind: "text"` — no hint depends on a highlight, an animation, or a region focus.

The prose teaches by explicit atom numbering rather than by pointing at figures ('Number the six carbons, so the ketones are at carbons two and five… Count the atoms enclosed by the new bond: carbons one, two, three, four, and five'). I searched the ten reader text blocks for colour words, 'shown above/below', and figure references and found none — the chapter's chemistry is genuinely carried by text.

No concept is assessed only by an inaccessible type. dieckmann-cyclization, the concept most at risk, pairs its two drawing items with two numeric_with_units items; aldol-reaction pairs its drawing items with single_select, bond_change_ledger and curved_arrow.

Unproduced video blocks are compiled with `is_hidden: true` and suppressed by the renderer, so the chapter exposes no dead 'Watch' links or empty media placeholders — the failure mode I expected to find given the empty `url` fields.
open_questions: The Ketcher embed is loaded as `/generator?embed=1&toolbarProfile=lti_drawing`. I could not determine from StructureWorkspaceRenderer alone whether that toolbar profile exposes a SMILES/text paste field inside the iframe. If it does, access-003 softens from 'impossible' to 'undiscoverable'; if it does not, the finding stands as written. This should be checked against the running embed rather than the source.

I inspected the LMS activity shell, the public question-set panel and the fifteen per-type renderers for a surface that consumes `accessible_description` and found none. I did not exhaustively audit the live-questions/exit-ticket path or any LTI-only view, so there is a small chance a delivery surface exists that I missed — that would downgrade access-001 but not access-002.

Several accessible descriptions say options are 'shown as structures'. Server-side visual enrichment does attach an `imageUrl` for each `structure_smiles`, so this is accurate in the activity shell — but the reader-side static preview file strips `student_config` entirely, so on that surface the phrase would describe something the student never receives. Worth confirming which surface students actually meet this bank on.

ch23-flawed-claisen's correct repair option `fix_two_h` runs about three times the length of either distractor. I judged this an item-writing tell rather than an access barrier and did not file it, but it is the kind of thing another persona may want to weigh.

personas.summary: Every figure in this chapter is chemically correct, legibly drawn, and actually reaches the compiled reader — I verified all 26 assets render cleanly with RDKit at reader-scale sizes, found no annotation_font_scale defect, no crowded or label-on-structure figure, and a 100% nugget-asset delivery rate. The problem is not figure quality but figure *kind*. All 36 molecule blocks are isolated single-species skeletal structures and there is not one relational figure in the chapter: no energy profile, no labelled atom, no numbered chain, no side-by-side comparison, no marked bond. This is the only chapter of the twenty-four in the reader with zero non-molecule figure blocks, and it has the highest molecule count of any of them — nine sibling chapters carry native `reaction_coordinate` blocks. Meanwhile the prose does an unusual amount of explicitly spatial work: it numbers carbons one through six across four sections, tells the student to count ring atoms as a bond forms, instructs them to draw resonance forms, instructs them to set an enol beside an enamine, and builds its entire thermodynamic argument on a coupled-equilibrium picture (unfavourable aldol pulled by irreversible dehydration) that is stated three times and drawn zero times. The substitution of per-species molecule figures for a `synthesis_roadmap` works for the Robinson annulation and the intramolecular aldol, where the species chain is complete and the reader can follow reactant to product; it fails for the Claisen (two figures for a section whose whole point is what happens at a tetrahedral intermediate that is never drawn), the Stork (the iminium the section warns you not to forget is never shown, though a question offers it as an option), and the Dieckmann (the six-membered case is argued in prose and asked about in a question but never drawn, while the structurally identical intramolecular-aldol section draws both ring sizes). No lone illustrated option acts as an answer tell anywhere in the 52-item bank — option sets are uniformly illustrated or uniformly textual, which is a genuine strength.

location.anchor_text: Dehydration is, for planning purposes, a one-way door.

findings.observation: The chapter's central thermodynamic argument — an unfavourable, reversible aldol addition coupled to an irreversible dehydration that drains the equilibrium forward — is carried entirely in prose and asserted in three separate sections (aldol reaction, dehydration, intramolecular aldol) without a single energy or equilibrium figure. The compiled reader contains 36 `molecule` blocks and zero `reaction_coordinate` blocks.
findings.learner_impact: A student is asked to hold two coupled equilibria, their relative depths, and the barrier that separates them in working memory purely from sentences. The claim that acetone gives 'only a few percent' at equilibrium yet 'good yield' of enone on heating reads as a contradiction until the two-well picture is constructed mentally; a student who cannot construct it takes the outcome on faith and cannot transfer the reasoning to the intramolecular-aldol ring-size argument, which reuses the identical logic.
findings.evidence: Reader prose: 'as long as some aldol product exists at equilibrium, and as long as it is consumed faster than it reverts, the addition equilibrium is continuously refilled and the whole system drains into the enone'; also 'Because dehydration is irreversible, the first product to reach that stage is the product you isolate' (nugget-intramolecular-aldol). Block census across frontend/public/reader/topic-chapters/: carbonyl-condensation.json = {molecule: 36, reaction_coordinate: 0}; nine other chapters carry reaction_coordinate blocks (alkenes-structure-and-reactivity 4, overview-of-organic-reactions 3, alkanes-and-stereochemistry 2, cycloalkanes 2, and five with 1). `reaction_coordinate` is an allowed topic-package asset type ([internal source reference — not in this repo] ALLOWED_ASSET_TYPES) that maps to a native reader block ([internal source reference — not in this repo]), not to the known-empty `image` path that `synthesis_roadmap` takes. The question set already ships exactly this profile: ch23-aldol-dehydration-profile encodes min 0.0 / TS 18.0 / min 4.0 / TS 20.0 / min -12.0 for the same acetone-to-enone sequence.
findings.recommended_outcome: The reader needs the coupled-equilibrium relationship — shallow reversible first well, deep irreversible second well — made visible at the point the argument is made, rather than existing only inside a graded question the student meets afterward. The renderer for this already works in this chapter's own question bank.

location.anchor_text: The bond formed is always donor alpha carbon to acceptor carbonyl carbon

findings.observation: The opening section establishes the one rule the whole chapter depends on — a bond forms between the donor's alpha carbon and the acceptor's carbonyl carbon, never between two alpha carbons or two carbonyl carbons — and illustrates it with four unrelated, isolated molecule cards (acetaldehyde, its enolate, benzaldehyde, but-3-en-2-one). No figure shows two partners together, shows which atom in each plays which role, or shows a bond between them.
findings.learner_impact: The section's single governing relationship is precisely the kind that a picture carries in one glance and prose carries in a paragraph. A student who reads 'finding those two atoms and drawing a line between them gets you most of the way there' is being told to do something visual and is given four structures with no indication of which atom on which molecule is meant. The four negative cases the prose rules out ('there is no version of this chemistry in which two alpha carbons bond to each other') are invisible.
findings.evidence: nugget-carbonyl-condensation-pattern asset_ids = [mol-acetaldehyde, mol-acetaldehyde-enolate, mol-benzaldehyde, mol-mvk]; all four compile to standalone `molecule` blocks (blk-v8n71yob, blk-4i1bteqz, blk-5v16arac, blk-g7rdpd6m) whose descriptions each characterise one molecule in isolation. Prose: 'When you are asked to predict a condensation product, finding those two atoms and drawing a line between them gets you most of the way there.'
findings.recommended_outcome: The donor-alpha-to-acceptor-carbonyl bond is the chapter's organising rule and needs to be visible as a relationship between two partners, not inferable from four separate structures. The overview section is where a student decides whether the chapter has one idea or seven.

location.anchor_text: Count the atoms enclosed by the new bond: carbons one, two, three, four, and five

findings.observation: Not one of the 26 figures in this chapter carries a label, a number, a highlight, or any annotation — every asset is a bare skeletal structure with rdkit_options limited to `show_hydrogens`. Yet the prose performs explicit atom-by-atom numbering in at least five sections (aldol product carbons 1-4, hexane-2,5-dione carbons 1-6, heptane-2,6-dione, diethyl hexanedioate carbons 1-6, the Robinson six-atom ring count, the Michael 1,5-relationship). The numbering scheme the prose relies on exists nowhere on the figures it refers to.
findings.learner_impact: The student must construct a numbered mental overlay on an unnumbered picture and keep it aligned across several paragraphs. Reading 'carbon five now bears an alkoxide, and it still carries its methyl group, carbon six, which hangs outside the ring' against an unannotated cyclopentenone requires re-deriving the numbering from scratch each time, and any misalignment silently corrupts everything downstream. This affects exactly the ring-counting skill that four questions assess (ch23-dieckmann-ring-size, ch23-mixed-aldol-product-count, ch23-match-diketone-to-ring, ch23-intramolecular-ring-product).
findings.evidence: All 26 assets in topic.package.json have rdkit_options of `null` or `{"show_hydrogens": true}` — no annotation, no highlight, no atom-note field is populated on any asset. Prose from nugget-dieckmann-cyclization: 'The new ring is bounded by the bond just made, and it encloses carbons two, three, four, five, and six: five atoms. Carbon one, the other ester carbonyl carbon, sits outside the ring.' The corresponding figures mol-diethyl-adipate and mol-ethyl-2-oxocyclopentanecarboxylate carry no numbering at all.
findings.recommended_outcome: Where the prose counts atoms, the figure the count refers to needs to carry that count, or the student needs some other way to see which atom the sentence means. This is the highest-leverage single change in the chapter because the same numbering discipline recurs in five sections and four questions.

location.anchor_text: The two reactions diverge at the tetrahedral intermediate.

findings.observation: The Claisen section carries only two figures — ethyl acetate and ethyl acetoacetate — the fewest of any section in the chapter, and they are the reactant and the product. The species the entire section is about, the tetrahedral intermediate and the difference between the aldol version (nothing to expel) and the Claisen version (an ethoxy leaving group), is never drawn. The one-versus-two-alpha-hydrogen requirement and the transesterification hazard, both given full paragraphs, are also unillustrated.
findings.learner_impact: The section explicitly frames itself as a comparison at a single branch point, and the branch point is invisible. A student must imagine two tetrahedral carbons side by side, differing in one substituent, from a sentence. The error_repair question then tests exactly this on ethyl 2-methylpropanoate — a structure that appears nowhere in the reader — so a student who did not build the mental picture has nothing to fall back on.
findings.evidence: nugget-claisen-condensation asset_ids = [mol-ethyl-acetate, mol-ethyl-acetoacetate] (2 assets; every other section has 3-5). The deferred video-claisen-mechanism storyboard requests exactly the missing picture: 'Zoom on the two intermediates: the left one carries only carbon and hydrogen, the right one carries an ethoxy group tinted as a leaving group.' Question ch23-flawed-claisen uses molecule_smiles `CCOC(=O)C(C)C` (ethyl 2-methylpropanoate), which has no counterpart figure in the reader.
findings.recommended_outcome: The addition-versus-substitution divergence is a two-structure comparison and needs to be visible as one; the section currently shows only the endpoints of a journey whose midpoint is the lesson.

location.anchor_text: Forgetting this final step is the single most common error on Stork problems

findings.observation: Two reaction intermediates are shown to students in the question bank but never in the reader: the Stork iminium salt (`CC(=O)CCC1CCCCC1=[N+]1CCCC1`, offered as intermediate m_iminium in ch23-stork-route) and the Robinson bicyclic ketol (`CC12CCC(=O)CC1(O)CCCC2=O`, offered as m_ketol in ch23-robinson-route). The Stork section explicitly warns that forgetting to hydrolyse the iminium is the commonest error, then never draws the iminium the student is supposed to remember to destroy.
findings.learner_impact: A student meets these structures for the first time in a graded synthesis-route item, where one is the correct intermediate and the other a distractor, without ever having seen either in the teaching text. The three-stage Stork sequence is the chapter's longest and the only multi-stage reaction with no video brief at all; its species chain in the reader runs cyclohexanone → enamine → (gap) → product, so the stage the warning is about is the one stage with no picture.
findings.evidence: nugget-stork-enamine-reaction asset_ids = [mol-cyclohexanone, mol-cyclohexenyl-pyrrolidine, mol-mvk, mol-2-3-oxobutyl-cyclohexanone] — no iminium. ch23-stork-route student_config intermediates include m_iminium with the iminium SMILES. nugget-robinson-annulation asset_ids = [mol-2-methylcyclohexane-13-dione, mol-mvk, mol-robinson-michael-adduct, mol-wieland-miescher-ketone] — no ketol. ch23-robinson-route intermediates include m_ketol. The five video_briefs cover aldol, E1cb, Claisen, conjugate addition and Robinson; none covers Stork.
findings.recommended_outcome: Where a section names a species as the thing students get wrong, and the assessment then shows that species as an option, the reader needs to have shown it first. The per-species-figure substitution for a roadmap works only when the species chain has no gaps in it.

location.anchor_text: Diethyl heptanedioate closes to the six-membered ethyl 2-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylate.

findings.observation: The intramolecular-aldol section draws all four structures of its 'add one carbon, grow the ring by one' contrast (hexane-2,5-dione, the cyclopentenone, heptane-2,6-dione, the cyclohexenone). The Dieckmann section makes the structurally identical argument and draws only the five-membered pair; diethyl heptanedioate and ethyl 2-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylate exist in prose only. The question ch23-dieckmann-ring-size then asks students for the ring size of the diethyl heptanedioate product.
findings.learner_impact: Two adjacent sections teach the same prediction rule with unequal support, so the harder of the two (Dieckmann, where the ring comes out one atom smaller than the carbon count suggests — a point the prose flags as 'one detail trips people up') gets the thinner visual treatment. A student is asked in assessment about a substrate-product pair they were never shown, in the exact case the chapter says is most error-prone.
findings.evidence: nugget-intramolecular-aldol asset_ids has 4 entries covering both ring sizes; nugget-dieckmann-cyclization asset_ids = [mol-diethyl-adipate, mol-ethyl-2-oxocyclopentanecarboxylate] only. Reader prose in the Dieckmann section: 'A 1,6-diester — six carbons counting both ester carbonyl carbons — gives a five-membered ring, and a 1,7-diester gives a six-membered ring. The ring always comes out one atom smaller than the carbon count suggests.' ch23-dieckmann-ring-size prompt: 'Diethyl heptanedioate is treated with sodium ethoxide in ethanol. How many atoms are in the ring of the cyclic product?' with student_config `{"placeholder": "number of ring atoms"}` — no structure shown.
findings.recommended_outcome: The two parallel ring-size arguments need parallel visual support, and the case the assessment tests needs to be one the student has seen. The gap is an asymmetry between two sections, not an absolute shortage.

findings.observation: Six assets are reused across sections, and each carries a single global `learning_goal` written for the section it first appeared in. In the reusing section the caption then describes something the section is not about. Ethyl acetoacetate appears in the Michael section captioned with the Claisen driving force ('the full equivalent of base deprotonates the product and drives the equilibrium forward') rather than with why pKa 11 makes it a Michael donor. Acetone appears in the mixed-aldol section captioned 'Ketone aldol additions are unfavorable at equilibrium; acetone at equilibrium is only a few percent converted' — irrelevant to that section, whose point is that acetone is the only enolizable partner present. 4-Hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one appears in the dehydration section captioned about how little of it forms, not about which H and which OH are lost.
findings.learner_impact: A student reading a figure caption that argues a different section's point either follows the caption away from the current argument or learns to stop reading captions. The mixed-aldol case is the most costly: the reader is being told to notice that acetone's equilibrium is bad at exactly the moment the section wants them to notice that acetone is the donor.
findings.evidence: mol-ethyl-acetoacetate learning_goal is Claisen-framed and is emitted verbatim as the description of blk-3jjyd5he inside the Michael section. mol-acetone learning_goal emitted verbatim as blk-kttdzh6y inside nugget-mixed-aldol-selectivity. mol-diacetone-alcohol learning_goal emitted verbatim as blk-o6td2g4a inside nugget-aldol-condensation-dehydration. mol-mvk carries one identical description across four sections (blk-g7rdpd6m, blk-3ibi68hy, blk-oa5q7r0v, blk-2rzp06bm).
findings.recommended_outcome: A figure reused in a second section needs its caption to say what it is doing *there*; a single global learning_goal per asset cannot serve two different arguments, and the compiler currently gives it no way to.

location.anchor_text: Set the whole set against ethanol at pKa 16 and the practical dividing line appears

findings.observation: The chapter builds a six-value acidity ladder (2,4-pentanedione 9, ethyl acetoacetate 11, diethyl malonate 13, ethanol 16, ketone 19, ester 25) with an explicit dividing line at ethanol, and uses it three times — to explain the Claisen driving force, to explain Michael donor selection, and to explain why the Stork route exists at all. It is never shown as a scale. `acid_base_energy_diagram` is an allowed asset type that compiles to the same native reader block as `reaction_coordinate`.
findings.learner_impact: 'Above or below ethanol' is a one-dimensional spatial relationship being carried by six numbers scattered across three sections. A student who cannot hold the ladder cannot see why the same dividing line explains a full equivalent of base in one section, monopoly of the donor role in another, and the whole purpose of an enamine in a third. The rank_order question ch23-rank-michael-donors asks the student to reproduce the ladder they were never shown.
findings.evidence: Reader prose (nugget-michael-reaction): 'Michael donors are the compounds already familiar as unusually acidic: diethyl malonate at pKa 13, ethyl acetoacetate at 11, 2,4-pentanedione at 9 … the same ordering holds for singly activated positions, where a ketone sits near 19 and an ester near 25. Set the whole set against ethanol at pKa 16 and the practical dividing line appears.' Also nugget-claisen-condensation ('pKa near 11 … five units below ethanol's 16') and nugget-stork-enamine-reaction ('A simple ketone at pKa 19 is not deprotonated to any useful extent'). [internal source reference — not in this repo]; [internal source reference — not in this repo] block.
findings.recommended_outcome: A one-dimensional ordering used as a decision rule in three separate sections needs to exist as an ordering the student can see once and refer back to, rather than as six numbers recited in prose.

location.anchor_text: That is two donors times two acceptors: four aldol products.

findings.observation: The mixed-aldol section is built on a problem-then-solution structure, and only the solution is illustrated. The four-product combinatorial mixture — two donors times two acceptors, two self-condensations and two crossed — is a 2x2 grid described entirely in words, while the three figures in the section (benzaldehyde, acetone, the clean Claisen-Schmidt product) all illustrate the case where the problem has already been solved.
findings.learner_impact: The student never sees the failure the whole section exists to prevent, so the payoff of the no-alpha-hydrogen strategy lands as an assertion rather than a relief. ch23-mixed-aldol-product-count then asks the student to enumerate that grid for propanal and butanal as a bare number with no scaffold, which is the one place where a picture of the grid would have done all the work.
findings.evidence: nugget-mixed-aldol-selectivity asset_ids = [mol-benzaldehyde, mol-acetone, mol-benzalacetone]. Prose: 'Call them A and B: you get A attacking A, B attacking B, A attacking B, and B attacking A. Four aldol products.' ch23-mixed-aldol-product-count student_config = `{"placeholder": "number of products"}`.
findings.recommended_outcome: The section needs the four-way mixture to be visible as a mixture, since the entire selectivity argument is about collapsing a grid from four cells to one and a grid is what the student is being asked to picture.

location.anchor_text: Drawing the resonance forms makes the consequence explicit

findings.observation: Resonance delocalisation is invoked as an explanation four times and drawn zero times. The enolate is shown only in its carbanion form (`[CH2-]C=O`), even though the chapter's opening sentence says the nucleophile's 'reactivity lives on carbon even though most of its charge lives on oxygen' — the oxygen-anion form is never drawn. The Michael section says in so many words that 'Drawing the resonance forms makes the consequence explicit' for but-3-en-2-one, and then shows but-3-en-2-one in one form with no second form and no partial-charge marking on the beta carbon.
findings.learner_impact: The reader is instructed to perform a drawing and given none, and the two-electrophilic-site claim that the whole Michael section rests on has to be taken on trust. A student who cannot generate the second resonance form has no way to see why the beta carbon is electrophilic, which is precisely the point ch23-michael-attack-site and ch23-michael-arrow assess.
findings.evidence: mol-acetaldehyde-enolate smiles `[CH2-]C=O`; its own alt_text concedes the limitation — 'drawn in its carbanion resonance form'. mol-mvk smiles `CC(=O)C=C` with rdkit_options `{"show_hydrogens": true}` and no charge markers. Reader prose (nugget-michael-reaction): 'Drawing the resonance forms makes the consequence explicit: alongside the usual form with positive character on the carbonyl carbon, there is a form with the negative charge on oxygen and the positive charge on the beta carbon.' The deferred video-conjugate-vs-direct-addition storyboard asks for exactly this: 'cycle its resonance forms, leaving partial-positive markers on both the carbonyl carbon and the beta carbon.'
findings.recommended_outcome: Where the prose tells the student that drawing a second form makes something explicit, the second form needs to exist somewhere the student can look at it; a single-form figure plus an instruction to imagine the other is the current state.

location.anchor_text: Compare it with an enol drawn beside it

findings.observation: The Stork section directs the reader to a side-by-side comparison that the reader does not contain: 'Compare it with an enol drawn beside it: the two differ only in whether the heteroatom is oxygen bearing a hydrogen or nitrogen bearing two alkyl groups.' No enol is drawn anywhere in the chapter, beside the enamine or otherwise.
findings.learner_impact: This is a literal instruction to look at something that is not on the page. The enol-enamine analogy is the section's whole conceptual bridge — it is how a student accepts that a neutral molecule can do an anion's job — and it is a one-atom structural difference, which is the single clearest case in the chapter where two adjacent pictures replace a paragraph.
findings.evidence: Reader prose, nugget-stork-enamine-reaction expanded text: 'Compare it with an enol drawn beside it: the two differ only in whether the heteroatom is oxygen bearing a hydrogen or nitrogen bearing two alkyl groups. Nitrogen is the better electron donor, which makes the enamine a distinctly better nucleophile than the corresponding enol.' Section asset_ids = [mol-cyclohexanone, mol-cyclohexenyl-pyrrolidine, mol-mvk, mol-2-3-oxobutyl-cyclohexanone]; the cyclohexanone enol (`OC1=CCCCC1`) is absent from all 26 chapter assets.
findings.recommended_outcome: The comparison the prose asks the student to make needs to be makeable; either the enol has to be visible next to the enamine or the sentence should stop instructing a comparison the page cannot support.

findings.observation: Three questions assess an explicitly structural skill using text-only compound names or condensed formulas, while their own twins in the same bank show structures. ch23-donor-or-acceptor-only asks students to sort six compounds by donor/acceptor role from names alone (including 'Diethyl carbonate', which appears in no chapter figure), whereas ch23-acceptor-only-partner asks the identical skill with all four options drawn. ch23-rank-michael-donors uses condensed text formulas (CH3COCH2COCH3). ch23-match-diketone-to-ring draws the four product rings but leaves the four diketones as names.
findings.learner_impact: The skill being tested is stated in the bank's own hints as a looking task — 'Find the carbonyl carbon first, then look only at the carbons bonded directly to it' — so removing the structure changes what is being measured from role-recognition to name-to-structure recall. A student who can do the chemistry but cannot draw diethyl carbonate from its name fails an item about condensation roles.
findings.evidence: ch23-donor-or-acceptor-only student_config items are `[{"id":"i1","text":"Acetone"}, … {"id":"i5","text":"Diethyl carbonate"}, {"id":"i6","text":"Cyclopentanone"}]` with no structure_smiles; ch23-acceptor-only-partner options all carry structure_smiles. ch23-rank-michael-donors cards are text-only condensed formulas. ch23-match-diketone-to-ring left column is text-only, right column carries structure_smiles on all four. Hint level 1 of ch23-acceptor-only-partner: 'Find the carbonyl carbon first, then look only at the carbons bonded directly to it.'
findings.recommended_outcome: Items that assess 'look at the structure and find the alpha carbon' need the structure present; the bank is internally inconsistent about this within a single concept.

findings.observation: ch23-robinson-retrosynthesis opens 'A target cyclohexenone is to be traced back to the two compounds that would build it by a Robinson annulation' and shows no target. The student_config is three text fields with no structure of any kind, and the accessible_description does not supply one either. ch23-robinson-statements-v2 similarly names cyclohex-2-enone as the acceptor without drawing it while drawing all five candidate donors.
findings.learner_impact: Retrosynthesis is a bond-breaking task performed on a picture. Asking a student to sequence three disconnections — undo the dehydration, undo the ring-closing addition, undo the conjugate addition — against a target that is only referred to means the reasoning is exercised abstractly and cannot be checked against anything. The answer options happen to be answerable from general knowledge, which makes the item easier than the skill it names.
findings.evidence: ch23-robinson-retrosynthesis student_config contains only `fields` (claim single_select, evidence multi_select, reasoning short_text); no start_structure, target_structure, or molecule_smiles. Contrast ch23-robinson-route, which does supply both start_structure (`CC1C(=O)CCCC1=O`) and target_structure (`CC12CCC(=O)C=C1CCCC2=O`).
findings.recommended_outcome: A retrosynthesis item that says 'a target' needs a target the student can look at and cut, or the stem should stop implying a specific structure is under analysis.

location.anchor_text: the enzyme aldolase performs precisely this cleavage on fructose 1,6-bisphosphate

findings.observation: The retro-aldol biology — aldolase splitting fructose 1,6-bisphosphate into two three-carbon fragments in glycolysis — is the chapter's one connection to a pathway a student may already know, and it is prose-only. Neither the sugar nor the cleavage site is shown.
findings.learner_impact: A one-sentence claim about a six-carbon sugar splitting at a specific bond has to be visualised from a name. The section's own transferable point — 'Recognizing the beta-hydroxy carbonyl pattern in a biological molecule is often the fastest way to see which bond a pathway is about to make or break' — is a pattern-recognition skill, and the example given is the one instance in the chapter where the pattern is not visible.
findings.evidence: nugget-aldol-reaction expanded text: 'In glycolysis, the enzyme aldolase performs precisely this cleavage on fructose 1,6-bisphosphate, splitting one six-carbon sugar into two three-carbon fragments.' Section asset_ids contain no sugar.
findings.recommended_outcome: The biological payoff rests on seeing a familiar pattern inside an unfamiliar molecule; either the molecule needs to be visible or the sentence should not promise a recognition the page cannot deliver.

findings.observation: The overview section's four figures are byte-identical reproductions of cards that appear again in the sections that own them (acetaldehyde and its enolate in the aldol section, benzaldehyde in mixed aldols, but-3-en-2-one in the Michael section). But-3-en-2-one is rendered four separate times with the same name, description and alt text. Across the chapter, 36 molecule blocks are generated from 26 distinct assets.
findings.learner_impact: Modest. Re-showing a structure where it is needed saves scrolling and is defensible. The cost is that the overview section spends all four of its figure slots on previews that carry no information the later sections do not repeat, at exactly the point identified in visual-002 where the section's own governing relationship goes unillustrated.
findings.evidence: blk-g7rdpd6m, blk-3ibi68hy, blk-oa5q7r0v and blk-2rzp06bm are four instances of mol-mvk with identical content. blk-v8n71yob / blk-1hjxj8yb (acetaldehyde) and blk-4i1bteqz / blk-uumiirt0 (enolate) are pairwise identical. Chapter totals: 36 molecule blocks from 26 assets, the highest molecule-block count of the 24 compiled reader chapters.
findings.recommended_outcome: The overview's figure budget should carry the overview's idea rather than preview four structures the chapter shows again anyway; this is a case for changing what a figure does, not for adding figures.

location.anchor_text: Two aldehydes, one new bond: the aldol reaction step by step

findings.observation: All five mechanism animations compile into the reader as `video` blocks with an empty `url` and `is_hidden: true`, so a student sees nothing. The production notes assert the substitution is covered — 'The reader carries the same content in nugget-X together with the figures' — but for three of the five that claim does not hold, because the figures show only reactants and products and the briefs are about intermediates and electron flow. This is a platform-wide state (no chapter in the reader has a produced video), but this chapter defers more of them than any other and its briefs specifically request the annotations findings visual-003 and visual-010 identify as missing.
findings.learner_impact: The multi-step sequences that motivated the briefs are left to prose plus endpoint structures. A student following the Claisen brief's promised comparison, or the Michael brief's promised resonance cycling, gets neither the animation nor a static equivalent of what it would have shown.
findings.evidence: All five video blocks in carbonyl-condensation.json (blk-d5tojv1k, blk-anvkzdmx, blk-9d675oza, blk-awacta2q, blk-2cwyvg99) have `"url": ""` and `"is_hidden": true`; all five briefs carry `production_status: deferred`. Census across all 24 chapters: 0 videos with a url. video-claisen-mechanism storyboard step 3 and video-conjugate-vs-direct-addition storyboard step 1 describe exactly the two missing static comparisons flagged in visual-004 and visual-010.
findings.recommended_outcome: Where an animation is deferred, the reader needs a static equivalent of the specific thing the animation was going to show — the intermediate, the resonance form, the labelled atom — rather than a claim that reactant and product figures already cover it.

strengths: Every one of the 26 assets renders correctly and legibly. I re-rendered all of them with RDKit at 300x220 and the six busiest at 420x330: no overlapping labels, no glyph sitting on a bond, no structure too small or too crowded to parse. The fused bicyclic Robinson product, the Michael adduct with two esters and a ketone, and the enamine all read cleanly at thumbnail scale.

No `annotation_font_scale` defect anywhere: all 26 assets carry either `null` or `{"show_hydrogens": true}` as rdkit_options, so the oversized-stereo-glyph failure mode does not occur in this chapter.

`show_hydrogens` is applied with judgement rather than by default — it is set on exactly the five small molecules where a student needs to count alpha hydrogens or see the carbanion (acetaldehyde, its enolate, acetone, but-3-en-2-one, (E)-but-2-enal) and omitted on everything larger, which keeps the bigger skeletons uncluttered.

Figure delivery is complete: all 26 nugget-referenced assets reach the compiled reader, with every nugget's asset_ids matching the reader section's molecule blocks one-for-one. Nothing is authored and then lost in compilation.

No lone-illustrated-option answer tell exists anywhere in the 52-item bank. Every multiple-choice and multi-select option set is either uniformly illustrated (4/4 or 5/5 with structure_smiles) or uniformly textual — the failure mode that made a single drawn option the giveaway in earlier chapters does not recur here.

The intramolecular-aldol and Robinson sections are the two places where the per-species-figure substitution for a roadmap genuinely works: both show an unbroken species chain (both diketones and both ring products; donor, acceptor, Michael adduct and final bicyclic enone), so a student can follow the transformation from the figures alone.

ch23-aldol-dehydration-profile ships a real, well-specified energy profile with labelled minima and transition states — proof that the platform renders this content properly and that the reader's total absence of energy figures is a choice rather than a capability limit.

The synthesis_route items (ch23-stork-route, ch23-robinson-route) carry both start and target structures plus structure-bearing intermediate options, so the two most sequence-heavy tasks in the bank are the two best-illustrated.
open_questions: The public reader preview file frontend/public/reader/topic-chapters/carbonyl-condensation.questions.json strips `student_config` from all 26 surfaced questions, so a stem like ch23-aldol-product-propanal ('Which structure is the aldol addition product?') reaches the preview panel with no structures at all. I verified this is identical across every chapter's .questions.json, so I have treated it as a platform gap rather than a chapter finding — but it means the chapter's best-illustrated items are unillustrated on the surface most students see first.

`reaction` is a supported reader block type with a `reaction_smiles` field ([internal source reference — not in this repo]) and the reader chapter builder maps it, but it is absent from ALLOWED_ASSET_TYPES in [internal source reference — not in this repo] — so a topic package currently cannot emit a reaction scheme even though the reader can render one, and no compiled chapter contains a single `reaction` block. If that is an oversight rather than a deliberate restriction, it is the cheapest available fix for visual-002 and visual-004.

Is `synthesis_roadmap` still known-broken? It compiles to an `image` block, which is the empty-render path the authors avoided, but `reaction_coordinate` and `acid_base_energy_diagram` compile to a native block and are demonstrably fine.
