location.anchor_text: a 1,4-diketone gives a cyclopentenone and a 1,5-diketone gives a cyclohexenone

findings.observation: This advanced matching item requires two moves the chapter never demonstrates. First, octane-2,7-dione must be mapped to a seven-membered ring, while the prose's stated rule covers only 1,4→cyclopentenone and 1,5→cyclohexenone and frames five- and six-membered rings as 'where this chemistry works'. Second, octane-3,6-dione requires choosing the terminal-side enolate over the internal ones to reach 3-ethyl-2-methylcyclopent-2-enone — but every worked example in the chapter deprotonates the terminal methyl of a methyl ketone, so the internal-versus-terminal decision is never modelled.
findings.learner_impact: I have been told twice that only strain-free five- and six-membered rings survive. Presented with octane-2,7-dione I either answer that no reaction occurs or force it into the six-ring answer, because the chapter gave me no seven-ring case. On octane-3,6-dione I pick an internal enolate, get a three-membered ring, decide I have made an error, and abandon the item.
findings.evidence: ch23-match-diketone-to-ring left items l3 'Octane-2,7-dione' → r3 3-methylcyclohept-2-enone and l4 'Octane-3,6-dione' → r4 3-ethyl-2-methylcyclopent-2-enone. blk-h8y0anu7 only works hexane-2,5-dione and heptane-2,6-dione and states 'five- and six-membered rings are where this chemistry works'. The seven-ring case is treated only in the undelivered practice_check of nugget-intramolecular-aldol.
findings.recommended_outcome: Ring cases and enolate choices that appear in assessment need to have been modelled at least once in the reading, including a ring size outside the five/six pair and an unsymmetrically substituted diketone.

location.anchor_text: Michael donors are the compounds already familiar as unusually acidic: diethyl malonate at pKa 13, ethyl acetoacetate at 11, 2,4-pentanedione at 9

findings.observation: One paragraph of the Michael section introduces, in sequence: three donor pKa values, nitrile and nitro activating groups, an ordering rule for doubly activated positions, an electronic explanation of why an ester is the weaker activator (the second oxygen's lone-pair donation), two more pKa values for singly activated positions, ethanol at 16 as the dividing line, a two-part consequence of that line, and then a five-member list of acceptor classes. That is roughly nine new ideas and six numbers in a single unbroken paragraph, with no table, no figure and no numeric line to look at.
findings.learner_impact: By the fourth pKa I have lost which number belongs to which compound. I skip the paragraph, which means I skip the one idea that makes the Michael reaction predictable, and I then cannot do ch23-rank-michael-donors or ch23-robinson-statements-v2, both of which are pure applications of it. This is the paragraph where I stop reading and start scrolling.
findings.evidence: blk-xkig4ddq, paragraph 3 (identical in _detail_texts.expanded). Downstream items depending on it: ch23-rank-michael-donors, ch23-rank-michael-donors-v2, ch23-robinson-statements-v2 (distractor d explanation cites pKa 25 versus ethanol 16), ch23-michael-attack-site.
findings.recommended_outcome: The pKa comparison that governs donor selection needs a form a student can hold at a glance rather than a run of numbers inside continuous prose.

location.anchor_text: the label for this is E1cb, elimination unimolecular conjugate base

findings.observation: E1cb is introduced, expanded and named in a single sentence, with no figure, no comparison to the E1 and E2 mechanisms the student already half-knows, and no drawing of the carbanion intermediate. The very next sentences then introduce the acid-catalysed E1 route with a carbocation at the beta carbon. Two elimination mechanisms with oppositely charged intermediates arrive in one paragraph and are immediately assessed at 'advanced' difficulty in a five-feature by two-case comparison matrix.
findings.learner_impact: E1 versus E2 was already the topic I did worst on. A third label, defined by an expansion of its acronym rather than by a picture, does not stick. When ch23-addition-vs-dehydration-v2 asks me to fill ten cells about which route passes through a carbanion and which through a carbocation, I flip a mental coin on each row rather than reasoning, and a wrong matrix gives me one generic paragraph with no indication of which cells failed.
findings.evidence: blk-59t2y57n paragraph 2 introduces E1cb and the acid-catalysed E1 route in consecutive sentences with no figure. ch23-addition-vs-dehydration-v2 is difficulty 'advanced' with 5 features × 2 cases and feedback_bundle carrying only generic_incorrect_explanation.
findings.recommended_outcome: A newly named mechanism needs to be shown, not only named and expanded, and ideally set beside the eliminations the student already has — especially before it is graded in a ten-cell matrix.

location.anchor_text: the resulting carbinolamine loses water under acid catalysis to give an iminium ion

findings.observation: The Stork section explicitly hands its first stage back to a prior chapter — 'Stage one is enamine formation, which is carbonyl chemistry from the aldehydes and ketones chapter' — and then uses 'carbinolamine' and 'iminium ion' as known vocabulary. Neither term is defined, and neither species is drawn anywhere in the chapter. The section's four figures are cyclohexanone, the finished enamine, MVK and the final product; every intermediate on the way in and on the way out is invisible.
findings.learner_impact: If enamine/imine formation is one of the things I did not master last chapter, this section is closed to me from its second paragraph. The chapter tells me the prerequisite exists but builds no bridge to it. When ch23-stork-route then asks me to choose 'the iminium salt from conjugate addition' as the middle intermediate, I am picking a structure whose class I have never seen drawn, and when ch23-stork-final-step-v2 asks which class of amine is required, I have no picture of what would go wrong with a primary amine.
findings.evidence: blk-mvfihhb7 paragraphs 2 and 4. Section assets: mol-cyclohexanone, mol-cyclohexenyl-pyrrolidine, mol-mvk, mol-2-3-oxobutyl-cyclohexanone. ch23-stork-route intermediate m_iminium (CC(=O)CCC1CCCCC1=[N+]1CCCC1) is the first iminium structure a student would ever encounter in this chapter — inside a graded item.
findings.recommended_outcome: The prior-chapter enamine/imine dependency needs an actual refresher with the carbinolamine and iminium shown, not a pointer to another chapter followed by undefined vocabulary.

location.anchor_text: the number of possible products collapses from four to one

findings.observation: Section 1 tells the student that with one non-enolizable partner the possible-product count 'collapses from four to one'. Section 4's expanded text corrects this to 'the product count drops from four to two — the crossed product and the self-condensation of the enolizable partner'. Section 4's standard text goes back to 'the product is a single conjugated enone'. The graded answer to ch23-mixed-aldol-product-count-v2 (acetaldehyde + benzaldehyde) is 2.
findings.learner_impact: I take my summary from the first section, because that is where the chapter told me the idea 'will come back in every section of this chapter'. Three sections later the number quietly changes and I do not notice, because the change is buried mid-paragraph. On the graded item I confidently type 1 and am marked wrong for a claim the chapter made to me first and most emphatically.
findings.evidence: blk-2y7y70ai final paragraph: 'the number of possible products collapses from four to one'. blk-h8wawbw9 paragraph 2: 'the product count drops from four to two'. _detail_texts.standard of nugget-mixed-aldol-selectivity: 'the product is a single conjugated enone'. ch23-mixed-aldol-product-count-v2 answer_key [redacted], tolerance 0.
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter needs one consistent account of how many aldol products a non-enolizable partner actually leaves possible, distinguished clearly from how many are synthetically isolated — the graded item turns on that distinction.

location.anchor_text: In glycolysis, the enzyme aldolase performs precisely this cleavage on fructose 1,6-bisphosphate

findings.observation: The aldol section's third stated learning objective is 'Use the reversibility of the reaction to predict the fragments of a retro-aldol cleavage', and the section closes with a paragraph asserting that 'Reversibility is not a nuisance to be engineered around; it is the point in biology', introducing glycolysis, aldolase and fructose 1,6-bisphosphate. No structure accompanies any of it, and no question in the 52-item bank assesses retro-aldol at all. The only retro-aldol practice is in the undelivered practice_check. The same pattern hits the Dieckmann section, whose third objective ('Connect the cyclic product to the alkylation and decarboxylation chemistry of beta-keto esters') is likewise unassessed while the prose invokes a 'six-membered cyclic transition state' and the acetoacetic ester synthesis in one sentence.
findings.learner_impact: I have no way to tell what matters. The glycolysis paragraph is written with the same weight as the mechanism, mentions three biochemistry terms and a sugar I cannot draw, and is followed by nothing that tests it — so I either burn study time memorising it or (more likely) skip it and then panic when an exam mentions retro-aldol. The chapter gives me no signal of importance anywhere: there are no objectives shown, no summary, and no emphasis markers.
findings.evidence: nugget-aldol-reaction.learning_objectives[2] and blk-10nbxf9y paragraph 4; no question_set has concept_slug aldol-reaction addressing the reverse direction (the eight aldol items are product prediction ×2, structure draw ×2, bond ledger ×2, curved arrow ×2). nugget-dieckmann-cyclization.learning_objectives[2] versus its four items (ring size ×2, draw product ×2). No learning_objectives reach the compiled reader (grep returns 0).
findings.recommended_outcome: Objectives the chapter states need either practice that matches them or a clear signal that they are background; and a struggling reader needs some visible statement of what the section is for.

location.anchor_text: The mechanism has three steps and no surprises.

findings.observation: The chapter repeatedly asserts that its content is easy or already known, in exactly the places where a weak student stalls: 'The mechanism has three steps and no surprises'; 'Nothing mechanistic is new here'; 'Counting the ring is a mechanical exercise'; 'Sorting the two roles is the whole skill'; 'Begin by seeing clearly why the naive mixed aldol fails'; 'it requires nothing new'; 'the alkoxide formed simply expels it again'; 'this chapter introduces no new mechanism'.
findings.learner_impact: Every one of those sentences is placed at a point where I am actually stuck. Being told that a three-step mechanism holds no surprises, immediately before I fail to reproduce it, tells me the problem is me and not the explanation. This is the tone that makes me stop asking questions in class, and it appears at least eight times across ten sections.
findings.evidence: blk-10nbxf9y ('three steps and no surprises'), blk-a9kb7040 ('Nothing mechanistic is new here'), _detail_texts.standard of nugget-intramolecular-aldol ('Counting the ring is a mechanical exercise'), blk-2y7y70ai ('introduces no new mechanism', 'Sorting the two roles is the whole skill' in the standard variant), blk-h8wawbw9 ('seeing clearly'), blk-venwqh8r ('it requires nothing new'), blk-xkig4ddq ('simply expels it again').
findings.recommended_outcome: Difficulty claims should be removed or inverted where the chapter is asserting ease about the exact step students most often fail; naming the step as hard and then supporting it does more for a low-confidence reader than declaring it easy.

location.anchor_text: a 1,6-diester closes a five-membered ring and a 1,7-diester a six-membered ring

findings.observation: The chapter uses at least four different counting conventions without ever tabulating them: 1,4-/1,5-diketone (carbonyl-to-carbonyl, inclusive); IUPAC locants (hexane-2,5-dione); 1,6-/1,7-diester (also carbonyl-to-carbonyl, but now the chain termini); and 1,2- versus 1,4-addition (counting from the oxygen). The result is that hexane-2,5-dione is a '1,4-diketone' giving a five-ring, while diethyl hexanedioate — the same six-carbon backbone — is a '1,6-diester' also giving a five-ring. The one sentence that explicitly warns about this trap exists only in the standard detail level and is absent from the default expanded text.
findings.learner_impact: Counting is the single operation this chapter asks me to do over and over, and the labels shift under me between sections. I try to build one rule ('subtract one from the number in the name') and it works for the Dieckmann and fails for the diketones. Because the warning sentence is not in the text I am shown, I never learn that there is a trap; I just keep getting ring sizes wrong on ch23-dieckmann-ring-size and ch23-intramolecular-ring-product and cannot see the pattern in my errors.
findings.evidence: _detail_texts.standard of nugget-dieckmann-cyclization: 'Ring size is the thing to be able to predict, and one detail trips people up... The ring always comes out one atom smaller than the carbon count suggests'. The rendered blk-a9kb7040 (expanded) omits this sentence entirely. Compare blk-h8y0anu7 ('a 1,4-diketone gives a cyclopentenone') with blk-a9kb7040 ('A 1,6-diester... gives a five-membered ring') and blk-xkig4ddq ('1,4-addition, counting from the oxygen').
findings.recommended_outcome: The chapter's counting conventions need to be stated together once, and the explicit off-by-one warning must appear at the detail level students actually read.

location.anchor_text: Run the ethyl acetate case in full.

findings.observation: In every one of the ten sections the compiled block order is: one large text block containing all four paragraphs, then all the molecule figures, then the links. Nothing is interleaved. The Claisen section's text block runs roughly 700 words before the first structure appears, and the structures that appear (ethyl acetate, ethyl acetoacetate) are the two compounds named earliest in the prose.
findings.learner_impact: When the prose says 'the tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate collapses, expelling ethoxide, to give ethyl 3-oxobutanoate — ethyl acetoacetate', I need to see ethyl acetoacetate at that moment. Instead I have to hold the name in working memory, keep reading two more paragraphs about pKa and stoichiometry, then scroll down and try to reconnect the picture to a sentence I have already lost. Integrating prose with structures is the thing I am worst at, and this layout maximises the distance between them.
findings.evidence: Reader section nugget-claisen-condensation: blocks are blk-6h9ci3tr (text, ~700 words), then blk-ao192sfe (ethyl acetate), blk-xb5nt87f (ethyl acetoacetate), then a hidden video and a link. The same all-text-then-all-figures pattern holds for all ten sections.
findings.recommended_outcome: Structures need to sit next to the sentence that names them; a 700-word block with the relevant picture four screens away is not usable by a reader who cannot hold structures in memory.

location.anchor_text: Match each symmetrical diketone with the cyclic enone it gives on treatment with base.

findings.observation: Only the option-based question types (single_select, multi_select) carry per-response wrong_answer_explanations. The nine other types in this bank — matching_pairs, rank_order, comparison_matrix, bond_change_ledger, categorize_groups, curved_arrow, structure_scaffold, structured_reasoning, synthesis_route, error_repair — supply a single generic_incorrect_explanation and nothing response-specific. On a four-pair matching item or a five-card ranking, a student who gets one element wrong receives the same paragraph as a student who got everything wrong.
findings.learner_impact: I answer a four-pair match, get told 'incorrect', and read a general paragraph about counting ring atoms. I have no idea whether I missed one pair or all four, or which. So I cannot repair anything — I just try again with a different guess. This is where I stop learning from the assessment and start gaming it.
findings.evidence: ch23-match-diketone-to-ring, ch23-rank-michael-donors, ch23-addition-vs-dehydration, ch23-aldol-bond-ledger, ch23-donor-or-acceptor-only all have feedback_bundle with generic_incorrect_explanation + hints and no wrong_answer_explanations array. The generic text is well written but is written for the whole item, not for a response.
findings.recommended_outcome: Multi-element items need feedback that identifies which element was wrong; a single item-level paragraph cannot diagnose a four-pair match or a five-card ranking.

location.anchor_text: whose climb measured from the valley immediately before it is larger than the first climb measured from the start

findings.observation: Both reaction_coordinate_reasoning items state the comparison that determines the rate-determining step inside their accessible_description, rather than describing the geometry and leaving the comparison to the student. v1: 'whose climb measured from the valley immediately before it is smaller than the first climb measured from the start'. v2: 'whose climb ... is larger than the first climb'. One of the four asked sub-answers (rate_determining_step) is therefore given away to anyone reading that description.
findings.learner_impact: As a struggling student I often rely on the text description rather than the picture, because the picture is the part I misread. Here the description hands me one of the four answers, which means I never practise the skill the item exists to build — and on an exam, where no description accompanies the diagram, I have not learned to measure a barrier from its own valley.
findings.evidence: ch23-aldol-dehydration-profile.accessibility_bundle.accessible_description and ch23-aldol-dehydration-profile-v2.accessibility_bundle.accessible_description, both compared against answer_key.expected.rate_determining_step (1 and 2 respectively).
findings.recommended_outcome: The description should convey the curve's shape and relative heights without performing the comparison the question asks for.

location.anchor_text: In this resonance form, which atom carries the negative charge? That is where the arrow begins.

findings.observation: Every hint in all 52 questions is kind 'text'. There is not one structure, highlight, or region-focus hint in the bank, including on the four curved_arrow items, the four structure_scaffold items, and the two matching_pairs items, where the difficulty is inherently about locating an atom on a picture.
findings.learner_impact: On ch23-aldol-attack-arrow my problem is not vocabulary — it is that I cannot find the alpha carbon on the drawn structure. A hint that says 'which atom carries the negative charge' restates the same words I already failed to map onto the picture. A hint that highlighted the atom would have unstuck me; three more sentences do not.
findings.evidence: All hints across topic.package.json question_sets have "kind": "text" (no structure/highlight/region kinds present anywhere). Affected: ch23-aldol-attack-arrow(+v2), ch23-michael-arrow(+v2), ch23-draw-aldol-product(+v2), ch23-draw-dieckmann-product(+v2).
findings.recommended_outcome: Items whose difficulty is locating an atom on a structure need at least one hint that operates on the structure rather than restating the prose.

location.anchor_text: Joining the wrong carbons: the new bond connects the alpha carbon of the donor to the carbonyl carbon of the acceptor

findings.observation: The package carries 30 authored trouble_spots (three per concept), naming precisely the wrong moves students make — joining alpha to alpha, using catalytic base for a Claisen, drawing the non-conjugated alkene, stopping at the iminium, running the Robinson stages in the wrong order. None of them reaches the reader as a labelled warning. Where the prose covers the same ground it does so as positive assertion embedded mid-paragraph, never flagged as 'this is the mistake'.
findings.learner_impact: I cannot distinguish a sentence that is telling me the rule from a sentence that is telling me the trap. 'there is no version of this chemistry in which two alpha carbons bond to each other' reads to me as one more fact among fifty, not as a warning about the error I am about to make. A named, visually distinct 'common mistake' is the thing I would actually copy into my notes, and there are none in this chapter.
findings.evidence: topic.package.json concepts[].trouble_spots — 30 entries; the compiled reader has no callout block type and no occurrence of the trouble_spot text. Reader block census contains only text, molecule, video, external_link, mcmurry_link.
findings.recommended_outcome: The authored common-mistake list needs to reach the student as something visibly distinct from the explanatory prose, at the point in the section where the mistake is made.

strengths: The wrong-answer explanations on the option-based items are the best scaffolding in the package: nearly every distractor is named for what it actually is ('This is the condensation product, formed after the aldol has lost water', 'This 1,3-dicarbonyl compound is the sort of product a Claisen condensation delivers'), so a wrong answer teaches rather than just marks.

Three of the four ring-counting walkthroughs (hexane-2,5-dione, heptane-2,6-dione, diethyl hexanedioate) number the chain explicitly and enumerate the enclosed atoms, which is exactly the level of step-by-step I need and rarely get.

Hint ladders genuinely scaffold rather than reveal: level 1 is almost always a procedural first move ('Find the carbonyl carbon first, then look only at the carbons bonded directly to it') and only level 3 approaches the answer.

The donor/acceptor framing in section 1 is a strong single organising idea, and the chapter really does return to it in every section, which makes the material feel like one thing instead of seven named reactions.

The distractor design is diagnostic rather than random — the aldol items consistently offer the condensation product, the wrong-connectivity isomer, and the Claisen-type product, so my particular error is identifiable.

The comparison_matrix and error_repair items ask me to reason about a plan rather than recall a fact, and their generic explanations model the reasoning well ('a step can only pull an equilibrium forward if its own reverse is negligible').
open_questions: The reader's detail-level slider defaults to 'expanded' and the three levels are mutually exclusive rather than cumulative. Is that intended? My blocker finding ss-001 assumes a student stays on the default; if the intended default is 'standard', the severity of ss-001 drops but the missing definitions still need to exist at every level.

The five video blocks compile with empty url and is_hidden true. I could not determine whether the reader suppresses them silently or renders an empty player — if the latter, that is an additional confusion point I have not scored.

The chapter and its question set both carry available: false, and counts.surfaced is 26 of 52 (variants staged). I reviewed all 52; if only the 26 non-variant items ship, ss-011 (ch23-rank-michael-donors-v2) and ss-012 (ch23-match-diketone-to-ring, which is a v1) may differ in reach.
I did not coin any new category ids; all findings use ids from the supplied list.

executive_summary: Baseline verdict is blocked, driven by two chapter-local chemistry blockers, two chapter-local delivery blockers, and the same three platform access blockers ch21 carries. The instructor persona verified every one of the 26 asset SMILES, every mass balance (aldol additions conserve formula, condensations lose exactly H2O, the Claisen loses exactly EtOH) and the Wieland-Miescher connectivity, and found the chapter's writing the strongest of the condensation series — but caught one error that formula checking structurally cannot catch: the chapter twice claimed octane-2,7-dione closes to a seven-membered ring, when the C3 enolate reaches C7 across only five atoms and the five-membered closure wins. Both candidate products are C8H12O isomers, so every automated check in the production pipeline passed. That claim also contradicted the chapter's own stated principle that reversible steps funnel into the strain-free closure, and the correct product was not among the matching options, so that item had no defensible answer. Separately the capstone Robinson worked example enumerated five ring atoms and called them six, and the acid-catalyzed dehydration had been written as a free secondary carbocation E1 — an error introduced during production's own coherence pass while fixing a different gap. All are corrected, along with a distractor bearing an impossible name and four definitions that existed only in a detail tier the reader does not show by default. Notably, the accessibility persona confirmed the ch22 answer-leak class was cleanly avoided: both profile descriptions were leak-free at baseline.
consensus_strengths: All 26 asset SMILES valid and every mass balance exact; the Wieland-Miescher product is correctly connected with the alkene at the ring fusion and the enone conjugation in the right place.
Both reaction_coordinate_reasoning descriptions were leak-free at baseline — the ch22 leak class was cleanly avoided.
No lone-illustrated-option answer tell anywhere in the 52-item bank; every option set is uniformly illustrated or uniformly textual.
Figure delivery is complete: all 26 nugget-referenced assets reach the compiled reader, one for one.
show_hydrogens is applied with judgement — set on exactly the five small molecules where a student must count alpha hydrogens, omitted on larger skeletons.
Nine of the fifteen question types are keyboard-complete in code; all 156 hints are text; every option carries a compound name alongside its structure.
No annotation_font_scale defect anywhere — the ch14/ch18 oversized-stereo-glyph failure mode does not occur.

ranked_recommendations.title: Correct the octane-2,7-dione ring-size claim
ranked_recommendations.need: The chapter twice keyed a 1,6-diketone to a seven-membered ring when a five-membered closure is available and wins.
ranked_recommendations.rationale: This is wrong chemistry with no defensible alternative reading, and it appeared both as a graded matching pair and as the section's own worked practice answer. The matching item is re-based on four substrates whose favoured closure is unambiguous; the practice check is re-based on nonane-3,7-dione; and the missing generalisation — count from every alpha carbon and take the smallest unstrained ring, not from the chain ends — is now stated explicitly, using octane-2,7-dione itself as the worked illustration.

ranked_recommendations.title: Correct the Robinson ring-atom enumeration

ranked_recommendations.title: Replace the free-carbocation account of acid-catalyzed dehydration

disagreements.topic: Whether the reaction-coordinate accessible descriptions leaked
